title: Hedging in Academic Writing
text:
Researchers rarely state their conclusions with absolute certainty. Instead, they tend to use hedges such as 'may', 'appears to', and 'it is likely that', which signal that a claim is tentative rather than proven. Such qualification protects the author against overstatement when the evidence is incomplete.

Critics, however, argue that excessive hedging can obscure the findings and make a text seem evasive. A study that repeatedly qualifies every result may leave readers unsure which claims the author actually endorses. Therefore, skilful writers balance caution with clarity.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do hedges such as 'may' signal?
options: That a claim is tentative rather than proven
That the author is certain of the result
That the study has been rejected

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what can excessive hedging do?
options: Obscure the findings and make a text seem evasive
Shorten the length of the study
Remove all uncertainty from the results

questions.text: What can be inferred about researchers who never use hedges?
options: They may risk overstating claims that the evidence cannot fully support
They always have complete evidence for every claim
They avoid writing academic papers altogether
They are unaware that hedging words exist

questions.text: Which conclusion best follows from the passage as a whole?
options: Effective academic writing needs a balance between caution and clarity
Hedging should be avoided in all academic texts
Readers prefer texts without any qualification
Critics have proven that hedging is always harmful

vocabulary.definition: cautious words that show a statement is not fully certain
a claim that says more than the evidence supports
avoiding a direct answer or clear position

paragraph_translations: Дослідники рідко формулюють свої висновки з абсолютною впевненістю. Натомість вони часто вживають застереження, такі як «may», «appears to» та «it is likely that», які сигналізують, що твердження є попереднім, а не доведеним. Таке уточнення захищає автора від перебільшення, коли докази неповні.

Однак критики стверджують, що надмірні застереження можуть затуманювати результати та створювати враження ухильності тексту. Дослідження, яке постійно уточнює кожен результат, може залишити читачів невпевненими щодо того, які твердження автор насправді підтримує. Тому вправні автори поєднують обережність із ясністю.
